newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow dive drives Australia stocks down at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow dive drives Australia stocks down at open.

text.p: The Australian sharemarket dived at the opening on Thursday, trailing a sharply weaker Wall Street lower with the banks hardest hit as the U.S. long bond yield spiked and local bond markets slumped.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 23.3 points to 2,336.0.
Brokers said traders had taken to heart the negative signals from offshore markets and there was little in the way of positive local news to compensate.
"We are playing follow the leader at the moment with the Dow down and U.S. rates up," said a Sydney broker, pointing to haemorrhaging in the big banks.
"National Australia Bank is taking a hiding even though it's improved from its start, but all the banks are down," he said.
The banks and finance index slid 1.7 percent early, compared to a drop in the key market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, of about one percent.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to two, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
